policies.title: Policies
policies.empty: No policies yet. Create one with "New policy".

create.title: New policy
create.intro: The policy is created inactive (version 1). Putting it in production is a separate, explicit activation step.
create.pdpRejected: The PDP rejected the policy document:
create.duplicateId: A policy with this id already exists.

fields.projectHint: Owning application. A policy belongs to exactly one.
fields.resourceTypeHint: Clean type name (e.g. document) — each app has its own namespace.
fields.actionsHint: Comma-separated verbs, or "*" for all (e.g. read, update).

rules.title: Rules
rules.noConditions: No conditions — the rule always applies.
rules.literalHint: Numbers and true/false are typed automatically; anything else is text.
rules.orderingNeedsNumber: Ordering operators (GT/GTE/LT/LTE) require a numeric value (ADR-023).
rules.advancedJson: This document nests deeper than the builder handles (more than 3 levels) — edit it as JSON.
rules.invalidJson: Invalid JSON — fix it before switching back to the builder.
rules.jsonHint: Full rules array. Switching back to the builder requires builder-compatible structures.

validation.rulesArray: Must be a JSON array of rules

lifecycle.activateIntro: Choose which version goes to production. Only this version will be evaluated.
lifecycle.deactivateIntro: Version {version} will be retired from production. History is preserved; nothing is deleted.
lifecycle.staleRevision: Another admin changed this policy while you were here. Reload to get the latest version, then retry — your input is kept.

edit.title: Edit policy — new version
edit.intro: Editing appends a new immutable version (v{version}), created inactive. The current version stays untouched; activating the new one is a separate step.
edit.fixedHint: Fixed — a policy keeps its id and app across versions.
edit.staleRevision: Another admin changed this policy while you were editing. Reload to bring the latest version, then retry — your changes are kept.

tester.title: Policy tester
tester.intro: Dry-run an authorization case with the same engine production uses. Pick the source: the ACTIVE policies, or a DRAFT you test without saving (R027).
tester.sourceHint: What the case is evaluated against.
tester.versionHint: Prefills the draft with this version (active or not).
tester.policyDraftHint: Paste a full document (a draft, or a saved version's JSON). Nothing is saved; the PDP validates it as if you were creating it.
tester.invalidPolicyJson: The policy document is not valid JSON.
tester.policyNotDocument: Paste the full policy document (policyId, resourceType, actions, rules…), not just the rules array.
tester.actionFormat: The action must look like resource:verb (with a colon), e.g. stepper:create.
tester.attributesHint: Attributes the rules read, e.g. assignees.
tester.subject: Subject (delegated)
tester.subjectHint: Leave empty to test as yourself; a different subject needs the delegation marker.

catalogue.title: Action vocabulary
catalogue.intro: Declare which actions exist for each resource type of an app. Authoring policies requires the vocabulary declared first (R028).
catalogue.appHint: Pick or type the app whose vocabulary you manage.
catalogue.appEmpty: Type an app above to view or declare its vocabulary.
catalogue.empty: This app declares no vocabulary yet. Add a resource type below.
catalogue.noStar: Do not use '*' here — the catalogue lists explicit actions.
catalogue.dupAction: That action is already in the list.
catalogue.alreadyExists: A vocabulary for that resource type already exists.
catalogue.actionInUse: You can't remove that action: active policies use it. Deactivate or re-version them first.
catalogue.stale: Another admin changed this vocabulary while you were editing. Reload and retry.

catalogueActions.pickFirst: Pick an app and resource type to see its actions.
catalogueActions.notDeclared: No vocabulary declared for '{resourceType}' in {app} — authoring here would 400.
catalogueActions.fallbackHint: Could not read the vocabulary; type the actions comma-separated.
catalogueActions.allPreview: Sends * → the PDP expands it to: {actions}

config.title: Per-app configuration
config.intro: Configure where subject attributes come from (claim mapping) and the PIP endpoint for attributes that don't travel in the token. It's optional: if absent, the system degrades, it never denies (R029).
config.appHint: Pick or type the app whose configuration you manage.
config.appEmpty: Type an app above to view or declare its configuration.
config.noneBody: {app} declares no configuration yet. This is a valid, safe state: subject attributes are taken from the token as-is and there is no PIP. Declaring it only adds capabilities; it is never required to evaluate.
config.saHint: Where to find each attribute inside the JWT. E.g. the app's roles live at resource_access.<app>.roles, not realm_access.roles.
config.pipHint: All-or-nothing: if you enable PIP, all four fields are required.
config.pipUrlHint: http(s) and must contain the {sub} placeholder (opaque Keycloak subject id).
config.pipCredentialHint: Just a name pointing at the deployment's secret mechanism. The secret (client secret, API key…) is never typed here and never touches the PDP store.
config.pipCredentialWarn: This looks like a secret, not a reference name. credentialRef is only an identifier; the secret lives in the deployment. Double-check before saving.
config.consumeNote: Today the claim mapping is only read by /permissions enumeration (R030); /evaluate does not consume it yet, and the pip block is resolved by no one until the R031 adapter. Configuring it now is correct, but it does not change evaluation yet.
config.vAtLeastOne: Declare at least one section: attribute mapping or PIP. To leave the app unconfigured, use Delete.
config.vAttrValue: Every attribute needs a claim path.
config.vPipUrlSub: The URL must be http(s) and contain the {sub} placeholder.
config.vPipCredential: credentialRef is required (a name, not the secret).
config.stale: Another admin changed this configuration while you were editing. Reload to bring the latest version, then retry — your changes are kept.
config.alreadyExists: This app already has a configuration. Reload to edit it.
